hints: Look closely at the grey muscle wall around G and around H. Which one has a much thicker wall and which one has a thin wall?
Remember which ventricle has to generate high pressure to pump blood all around the body, and so needs the thickest myocardium.
walkthrough:
**Observe the section**

This is a transverse section through the ventricles. You can see two cavities surrounded by muscle (the grey area).

Chamber H is surrounded by a very thick muscular wall. Chamber G is surrounded by a much thinner wall.

**Apply the ventricle wall rule**

The left ventricle pumps blood to the whole body via the aorta. That needs high pressure, so it has a very thick wall.

The right ventricle only pumps blood a short distance to the lungs. That needs low pressure, so it has a much thinner wall.

**Identify G and H**

The thick-walled chamber H must be the left ventricle. The thin-walled chamber G must be the right ventricle.

That matches G = right ventricle and H = left ventricle.

options.A: This swaps the sides. H has the thick wall, so H is the left ventricle, not the right.
options.B: Both chambers are ventricles in this section, not atria. Atria have very thin walls and are found higher up in the heart.
options.C: G is a ventricle, not an atrium. It is the thin-walled right ventricle.
options.D: Correct. G is the thin-walled right ventricle and H is the thick-walled left ventricle.
